How to bounce back
from a wasted year
Stop calling it wasted. You learned what doesn't work, what you don't want and who your real friends are. That's not nothing.
Pick one big goal for the next twelve months. Health, money, a skill, a project. One clear target beats ten vague resolutions.
Break it into weekly steps. A goal for the year becomes fifty-two small actions. Each week, you only need to win that week.
Fix your daily basics first. Sleep, food, movement. With a solid base, everything else becomes much easier. Start with sleep.
Before: I felt I had lost a whole year. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and every day now feels like progress.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: I felt I had lost a whole year. After: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Every day now feels like progress.

slides.texte_overlay: Find someone to keep you accountable. A friend, a coach, a training partner. Telling someone your plan makes you far more likely to follow it.
Celebrate the first month. Look back after thirty days and notice what changed. Momentum is built by seeing your own progress.
